dedupe_keys.name: solar farms mapping models and inference

description: Microsoft publishes code for training and applying a solar-farm segmentation model to Sentinel-2 imagery. The repository documents training, tile inference and large-area inference, links a pretrained checkpoint, and provides notebooks for detection and construction-date or land-cover analysis. Its documented application covers India; transfer to another region requires suitable imagery and checks on detection quality. Python source and a Conda environment are available on GitHub under the MIT licence at no cost, while the accompanying geometry data have separate terms. The model can help prepare generation-asset inventories for exposure and capacity simulations, complementing data-harmonised-global-wind-solar-farm-locations-osm. A caveat is that the provided environment uses older PyTorch and geospatial-library versions, and inference still requires imagery and model weights. The checkpoint link was identified but its file was not downloaded. Neither detection accuracy nor cross-country transfer was tested, and mapped panels do not directly establish electrical capacity.
